classification.difficultyReason: Substitutes two defined differences and simplifies reciprocal expressions to recognise a cotangent difference identity.

answer.short:
$\frac1p+\frac1q=\frac{1+\tan\alpha\tan\beta}{\tan\alpha-\tan\beta}=\cot(\alpha-\beta)$.

Substitute for $p$ and $q$, use reciprocal identities and recognise the tangent difference expansion.
answer.worked:
Using reciprocal identities,
$$\begin{align*}q&=\frac1{\tan\beta}-\frac1{\tan\alpha}\\q&=\frac{\tan\alpha-\tan\beta}{\tan\alpha\tan\beta}.\end{align*}$$
Starting from the right-hand side,
$$\begin{align*}\frac1p+\frac1q&=\frac1{\tan\alpha-\tan\beta}+\frac{\tan\alpha\tan\beta}{\tan\alpha-\tan\beta}\\\frac1p+\frac1q&=\frac{1+\tan\alpha\tan\beta}{\tan\alpha-\tan\beta}\\\frac1p+\frac1q&=\frac1{\tan(\alpha-\beta)}\\\frac1p+\frac1q&=\cot(\alpha-\beta).\end{align*}$$
